body:
MYK'S CALL. Two landed positions conflict, and building the sixth roster verb requires choosing between them. I stopped rather than choose.

THE CONFLICT.
- T263 (SPEC §58 position 3) decided: "a peer's RENDERER blessable behind glass under the envelope, resolvers never (DECIDED)". The sixth verb of the container roster is `bless-renderer`, and the subtree-walls rail names it as owed: "a resolver arriving on the connection's channel stays inert and its bless attempt refuses, and a renderer it blesses serves behind glass under its envelope".
- T209 (SPEC §46.5) decided the opposite, and rails it: `test/federation/install-by-federation.test.ts:1599` asserts `names.filter((n) => n.includes("bless")).toEqual([])` over the WHOLE tools list. Its comment states the reason: "tools are the unit of CONSENT, and mounting a stranger's code is not a consent a connector token may give."

That rail is frozen (T209 is archived), and it fails the moment any tool with `bless` in its name is offered, whoever is asking.

WHAT I BUILT AND REVERTED. `loam_container_bless_renderer`, fenced with `channelAdmits` so a connection mounts only from a channel its own container opened, driving the shipped `blessChannelApp` (which already carries `expect: "renderer"`, `dependencies: "refuse"` and `manifest: "operator"`), never `blessChannelResolvers`. It reported the container's envelope and refused to announce a mount that does not serve. It works; it breaks the T209 rail; I reverted it.

THE READING THAT RECONCILES THEM, offered as a recommendation and not a decision. T209's caller is an OPERATOR TOKEN. A bound connection is a different thing: a person sat at a consent page and approved this connector for this container, which is exactly the consent §46.5 says a connector token cannot give on its own. So the rule could be: no tool mounts a stranger's code for an unbound caller, and a BOUND connection may mount a renderer into its own container, behind glass, under its container's envelope.

THAT NEEDS THE TOOL LIST TO BE PER-IDENTITY, which it is not today: `MCP_TOOLS` is one constant served to everyone. Making the roster's bless verb visible only to a bound caller satisfies T209's rail as written and delivers §58's capability. It is a real design change to the door, not a rename.

THE OTHER TWO ROADS, so the choice is a real one:
- Amend T209's position in the spec and re-authorize its rail through the vocabulary-rename road. Honest, but it changes what §46.5 promises.
- Drop `bless-renderer` from the roster. §58 keeps five verbs, and mounting a peer's renderer stays the CLI's alone. Cheapest, and it costs an agent the ability to finish what it started.

Acceptance criteria (whichever road you pick):
(a) The chosen position is written in the spec, and the position it supersedes says so. Verify: the spec section, and a rail naming both.
(b) An unbound caller can never mount a peer's code, by any tool name. Verify: test/federation/install-by-federation.test.ts, unchanged and green, or its successor asserting the same for an unbound caller.
(c) If a bound connection may mount: it mounts only from a channel its own container opened, only a renderer and never a resolver, the route serves under the container's envelope and not the operator's, and a blessing that lands without serving is reported as not mounted. Verify: a new rail, two-sided at each clause.

Merge tier: MYK'S. This decides what the system promises about running a stranger's code.
title: Two landed positions disagree about whether a tool may mount a peer's code
